featured_reviews.name: Farheen Darwesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I've been passing by the restaurant on the regular and always wanted to try it out. Honestly, I don't know why we didn't come here before. And now that we have, it's hand's down my favourite Sea food restaurant, in this part of town.

I really liked the whole vibe of the place, especially the hand painted murals on the 1st floor seating area. Comfortable seating, spacious yet cosy.

Their speciality being Mangalorean cuisine, we obviously had to try the staples! So we started with their superb Prawns Rava fry, coated and shallow fried in the most crunchy rava coating, is a must have. It was so good we ordered 3 plates! Same goes for their Prawns Koliwada fry, with delicious crispy bits of curry patta, adding an amazing punch of flavour! Both these come highly recommended by everyone.

You also must try their 'Sukkha Masala' - with any seafood of your choice. We went for their Teesria or clams. The masala has a heavy dose of fresh grated coconut, spices and well balanced flavors.

For the mains, Please do not leave without trying their Ghee Roast. It's the best I've had in Bombay. Right up there with the famous one from Nagarjuna, Bangalore.  Perfect roast masala with liberal amount of cashews in it. Best eaten with Neer Dosas. I just wish their quantity was a little more. It's just enough for one good eater.

The Prawn Gassi with Kori Roti is another Mangalorean speciality you cannot miss! Their Fish thalis are also very good and reasonable too.

The verdict: Superb food and good service are a delightful combination!

UPDATE: Visited the last two times and I'm sad to say that they lost the title for the best ghee roast. Since the chef changed, the dish is very mediocre, with maybe two-three bits  of cashews in it. :( Taste is not right too

description:

Not as renowned as a Malvan Katta Lunch Home offers seafood cooked in the traditional malvani style, and becomes an instant favourite thanks to its remarkably delicious taste. The options are aplenty: right from Tisriya Sukha, to Prawns sukke, to Surmai Masala and even Baby Sharks. However, if you’re one with an appetite, they also serve the best seafood thalis, which are just as delicious!

As you can imagine, this is home-style dining at its finest and Malvan katta not catering to anyone’s tastes but he and his family’s so expect hearty, coconut-y flavours and plenty of masala spices.

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ Highly Recommended for Authentic Maharashtrian & Seafood Lovers! ⭐

Hotel Malvan Katta, located at Vikhroli West on LBS Marg, just opposite HCC, is a must-visit place for anyone who enjoys authentic Maharashtrian and Indian seafood.

We tried a variety of fish thalis, and the taste and quality were excellent and truly commendable. The food felt fresh, flavorful, and homely. The prices are very reasonable, especially for thalis, biryani, and other menu items.

We also tried the mutton keema thali and chicken suka thali, both of which were very delicious and reasonably priced. A big plus is that in the thali, you get options of chapati as well as bhakri, which perfectly complements the authentic Maharashtrian flavors.

The quantity is impressive—we tried prawns biryani, boneless chicken biryani, and also explored the veg menu. Dishes like veg biryani, veg pulao, and paneer biryani were absolutely delicious and served in generous portions.

Great food, great flavours! We went here for lunch on a Friday afternoon  - it was quite packed - recommend reservation.

We ordered: Bombil fry and Surmai for starters. Followed by Prawns Gassi, Rawas Pulimunchi with Neer dosa and Malabar paratha. I personally liked the curries with the neer dosa better. We finished off with kulfi and caramel custard for dessert.

featured_reviews.review_text:

What I like even more about this branch compared to others is how spacious it is. It feels more comfortable to dine in, with enough room that you don’t feel too cramped or rushed, even when there are a lot of customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Parida
featured_reviews.review_text: It is one of the best restaurant for sea foods. We had tasted here squid, lobster, crab soup, surma, pomphret, Bombay duck. All items are tasty, service also very fast. One may select the fish prior to cooking also.

featured_reviews.name: VIBHUTI SIRSAT
featured_reviews.review_text:

The food, service, and ambiance are all incredible. We had a perfect time—the dishes were delicious and the atmosphere is stunning and perfect for groups. Seriously, every corner is Insta worthy! Highly recommend for a fun night out with friends.

featured_reviews.name: SHIRLEY GAIKWAD
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wouldn’t recommend this place.
I visited after a long break, hoping for the same experience Mahesh was once known for, but it was extremely disappointing. The ghee roast tasted odd, and the masalas were clearly undercooked. I felt nauseous after eating it. The soups were bad too, they tasted burnt, and even after asking for a remake there was barely any improvement.
The restaurant is expensive, which wouldn’t be an issue if the food justified the price, but this was absolutely ridiculous.
The neer dosa was raw and felt like one dosa had been cut in half and served as two. The squid was just about bearable, but by then the overall experience had already ruined the meal.
We left feeling completely disappointed. What made it worse was that even after complaining to the manager, nothing was done to address our concerns.
Mahesh used to be much better. Sadly, that quality is gone now.
Please save your money and skip this place.

Well, lve lived in Vikhroli for 21yrs and left this place in 2010 but what gets me back here time and again and again is THIS RESTAURANT... MAHARASHTRA LUNCH HOME.

featured_reviews.name: foodie_namz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today had been to Maharashtra Lunch home to try their Veg thali. The place was very nice and welcoming.
The thali included soft phulkas served with a well-spiced dry Baigan sabzi and a flavourful aloo mutter gravy. The yellow dal and rice were comforting.
It was accompanied by fresh onion salad, crispy roasted papad, sol kadhi which enhanced the overall taste and variety on the platter. The gulab jamun served at the end was warm and perfectly sweet, making for a delightful finish.

A wholesome and well-balanced meal for anyone looking to enjoy a traditional Indian thali with homely flavours.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic Seafood Soul Food in Vikhroli!

If you are craving a proper Maharashtrian seafood feast, this place is a gem. We recently tried their Pomfret Thali, and it was an absolute delight.

The Pomfret: The star of the show. We had both the Pomfret Fry and the Pomfret Curry. The fry was perfectly crisp on the outside with a flavorful masala coating, while the fish remained juicy inside. The curry had that authentic coastal tang and spice balance that pairs so well with rice.

The Rice: They serve Indrayani Rice, which is a game-changer. It’s sticky, aromatic, and has that homely feel that elevates the entire meal.

Accompaniments: The thali comes with Bhakri, which was soft and fresh—perfect for soaking up the curry.

Vibe: It’s a classic "lunch home" setup—clean, no-frills, and focused entirely on the quality of the food. Great for a hearty weekend lunch.

Rating: 4.5/5
Must try: Pomfret Thali with Indrayani Rice.

featured_reviews.name: Maharashtrian traveller
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Delightful Dining Experience

We visited the **Maharashtrian Lunch Home – Vikhroli branch**, and the dining experience was exceptional, offering rich flavors and a thoughtfully curated ambiance. The atmosphere was calm, cozy, and elegantly designed, with walls decorated with sketches of Maharashtrian village life that added a beautiful cultural touch.

For those unsure about what to order, the staff is attentive and helpful—do ask for their recommendations.

The **Surmai Thali** was a standout, featuring fresh, perfectly cooked fish with authentic coastal flavors. Each element in the thali complemented the other, making it a satisfying and wholesome meal.

The **Chicken Thali** was equally impressive, with tender, well-marinated chicken prepared in flavorful gravy, paired with well-balanced sides. The portion size was adequate for one person and quite fulfilling.

While the pricing is slightly on the higher side, the quality of food and the peaceful ambiance make it worth it.

This restaurant is a great choice for anyone looking to enjoy authentic flavors in a relaxed setting.

featured_reviews.name: Sapaatu Payanam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just visited Mejwani Maharashtrichi in Powai, Mumbai for lunch and it turned out to be a proper Maharashtrian feast! If you love authentic regional food, this place is definitely worth trying.

Started the meal with Kothimbir Vadi – perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, packed with coriander flavor. A classic Maharashtrian snack done right.

Next came the Chicken Pahadi and Kabab. The Chicken Pahadi had a nice smoky flavor with mild spices, while the Kabab was juicy, tender, and grilled beautifully. Great starters to kick off the meal.

For the main course, I tried Valacha Birda and Maswadi. Valacha Birda, a traditional Maharashtrian curry made with field beans, had a rich, earthy taste. Maswadi was unique and flavorful, with its spiced gram flour dumplings soaking up the curry perfectly.

Paired everything with Jawari Bhakri, which tasted fresh and authentic – a perfect match for the curries. Also had Green Salad and Steam Rice on the side to balance the meal.

Ended the lunch on a sweet note with Kharvas, a traditional Maharashtrian dessert made from colostrum milk. It was soft, mildly sweet, and flavored with cardamom – the perfect way to finish the meal.

Overall, a satisfying experience with authentic flavors that truly represent Maharashtrian cuisine. If you’re in Mumbai and want to try traditional dishes beyond the usual restaurant menus, this place is definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Stephen Antu Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this place to watch the T20 Men’s World Cup Final, and overall the experience was a bit of a mixed bag.
The food was good and reasonably priced, and the ambience was okay. Nothing extraordinary, but decent enough for a casual evening.
Where things became disappointing was the beverage pricing and transparency. A 330 ml draught beer at ₹289 felt fair, but Old Monk priced at ₹179 for just 30 ml is extremely overpriced. The menu also lists Old Monk 180 ml at around ₹899, but nowhere in the menu is it mentioned that this price is a discounted bundle or special pricing.
Because we're paying through District, we were only allowed to order the 30 ml measure at ₹179, not the 180 ml option. While it’s clearly mentioned that two offers cannot be clubbed (which is understandable), the menu never explains that the 180 ml price itself is already a discounted rate, which makes the pricing structure quite confusing.
Another small but annoying point was that regular drinking water wasn’t available, so we had to purchase bottled water priced at ₹79 for 1 litre.
Considering the premium beverage pricing, the service and upkeep didn’t feel very premium. The seat we were given was stained and not properly cleaned, and overall the service didn’t match the pricing expectations. If beverages are priced at a luxury level, one would also expect better grooming standards from the staff and better maintenance of seating.
We had also reserved a table through District, but at the reception we were still asked to write down our name and phone number, which made it seem like reservations weren’t really being checked.
Since we went there specifically to watch the match, another small detail was that the rooftop projector and screen weren’t properly aligned.
That said, despite all these issues, we still managed to enjoy ourselves, and the highlight of the evening was India winning the World Cup, which definitely made the night memorable.
With better pricing transparency, maintenance, and service standards, this place could offer a much better experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Taste of Malvan in Powai, and honestly, it did not live up to the expectations of a Malvani restaurant at all. I visited on a Sunday night, and the place was almost 90% empty—which in hindsight should have been a clear sign to skip it. Unfortunately, I still decided to try it, and it turned out to be a complete mistake.

Starting with the food, the quality was extremely poor and far from authentic Malvani cuisine. Malvani food is known for its rich flavors, freshness, and bold use of spices, but what was served here felt careless and poorly prepared. The prawns butter garlic was one of the worst I have had—bland, lacking freshness, and completely disappointing. The surmai fish was another letdown; it was sliced extremely thin and did not feel like a proper serving. The taste and texture were both underwhelming.

I also ordered chicken vade, and that was equally disappointing. The vade dough clearly tasted frozen and stale. Anyone who has had fresh homemade vade can easily tell the difference—I personally can because my mom cooks vade at home, and the contrast was very obvious. What was served here lacked freshness, softness, and authenticity.

What made it worse is that the food overall did not taste fresh at all. In fact, I would say roadside food stalls serve much better and fresher Malvani food than this restaurant. That says a lot about the quality being offered here.

The only positive aspect was the service. The staff was polite, humble, and attentive, which I genuinely appreciated. However, good service alone cannot make up for such poor food quality.

Spending around ₹3500 on this meal felt like a complete waste. For that price, you expect good quality and authentic flavors, but instead, the experience was extremely disappointing.

Ruined Evening – Terrible Service & Absolute Lack of Basic Etiquette
​Rating: 1/5 stars
​We had an incredibly frustrating experience at Pop Tate's. While the food was okay, the service was outright appalling and completely ruined our evening.
​We arrived when the restaurant was busy, but even after it emptied out, we ended up sitting there for almost three hours due to pure negligence.
​The Food and the Missing Ingredients:
We ordered the jalapeno cheese balls, but they were served completely missing the jalapeno. When we pointed this out, the server offered to replace it with an avocado alternative... which never even arrived.
​The 1-Hour Delay & Lazy Excuses:
I had to follow up with our server three times about our order. After waiting for over an hour, the server's explanation was that the KOT (Kitchen Order Ticket) hadn't printed in the kitchen. What makes this unacceptable is that the server lacked the basic courtesy to check on the delay or inform us beforehand. I eventually had to ask a completely different server just to find out what was happening, and nobody seemed to have a clue. This is exceptionally poor etiquette from the service team.
​Frustrating "Apology":
At the end of the night, the head server came over with a complimentary pastry to apologize. We politely declined, explaining that the team had already ruined our evening and that they needed to train their staff to pay attention to tables and anticipate guest needs. Instead of listening, the server didn't even apologize verbally and simply brought the pastry again after we had already denied it. This just added to our frustration.
​Final Verdict:
Throughout the night, the servers were completely preoccupied chit-chatting with each other instead of managing their tables. I highlighted this directly to the head server. This branch desperately needs strong, strict supervision and heavy retraining for its staff. I sincerely hope management takes this seriously and improves in the near future, but as of now, I cannot recommend this place.
